target_customer: Developers and product teams at companies that embed live video and audio calls in their apps
problem: Building reliable real-time video calls on WebRTC is slow and hard; Dyte offered SDKs to add calls in a few lines of code.
business_model: Usage-based API and SDK pricing (per participant minute, with a free tier)

founders.name: Palash Golecha
founders.background_notes: Based in Bengaluru per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Wrapping WebRTC with cross-platform SDKs, scaling media servers and low latency is standard but nontrivial infrastructure engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Many video API vendors existed and developers can switch; some integration lock-in once SDKs are embedded.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Larger infrastructure players kept competing; Cloudflare, which lacked a client SDK, absorbed Dyte and launched RealtimeKit in April 2025 built with Dyte.

market_need_then: The 2020 shift to remote work and virtual events raised demand for embedded video; the company claims integration in under 10 lines of code.

branding.domain_note: Used dyte.io, not .com; later redirects to Cloudflare Realtime after acquisition.

identity.visual_style: Rocket emoji used in the tagline
identity.voice_and_tone: Developer friendly and playful (rocket emoji in tagline)

brand_strength.rationale: A search found no press on the brand itself; mostly its own SEO comparison blog posts.

outcome_analysis: Dyte was founded in 2020 in Bengaluru, joined YC in Winter 2021 and raised an 11.6 million dollar seed in April 2022 led by Unbound, Surge and Nexus. It reached a sale to Cloudflare, which one analyst framed as an acquihire to gain a client SDK; Cloudflare launched RealtimeKit with Dyte in April 2025. The price was not disclosed and the product is now folded into Cloudflare.
notes: dyte.io now redirects to cloudflare.com/products/realtime. Acquisition date not stated in sources seen; 2025 is inferred from Cloudflare Realtime launch in April 2025. Venture Intelligence says about 15M total raised from Nexus, Peak XV, Unbound and YC between July 2021 and April 2022; only the 11.6M round has a stated breakdown. Competition list empty: only undated vendor comparison pages found (Twilio, Agora, 100ms, Daily named in Dyte blog).
